characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku X-ray diffractometer, Cu-Kα source, 40 kV, 15 mA, scan rate 5° min−1
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 400 °C the deconvoluted (110) region resolves a BCC component, a B2-type component and a γ-brass type component; no Fe5Si3-type silicide phase is present at 400 °C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Ex-situ XRD of annealed powder; full pattern 2θ = 20–100°, enlarged (110) region 42–46°
characterization_methods.purpose: To study the phase evolution/thermal stability of the 35 h milled powder after annealing at different temperatures

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GSAS-II (general structural analysis system); pseudo-Voigt profile function, Chebyschev-I background with 10 coefficients
characterization_methods.key_findings: 400 °C annealed: BCC 57.00 % (a = 0.286 nm, 21 nm), γ-brass type 21.30 % (a = 0.872 nm, 12 nm), B2 21.70 % (a = 0.289 nm, 18 nm); refinement quality wR = 2.088, GoF = 1.05, χ² = 1.10.
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine the phase fraction, lattice parameter and crystallite size (and microstrain/dislocation density) of the annealed sample

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Pressure = 100000.0 Pa, system size = 1.0 mol, mole fraction Mn = 0.19, Ni = 0.15, Al = 0.15, Si = 0.1, C = 0.01; temperature range 25–1200 °C (property diagram 600–1500 K)
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD modelling (property diagram and single-point equilibrium calculation)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: CALPHAD-predicted phases were correlated with the experimentally observed phases of the annealed and SPSed samples; differences were attributed to the use of the TCFE8 database instead of TCHEA3.

processing_steps.atmosphere: toluene as process control reagent (to avoid oxidation)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Starting elemental powders of Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si and C (99.2% pure) in proportion Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 (at.%; Fe-46.00, Mn-21.50, Ni-18.13, Al-8.34, Si-5.78, C-0.25 wt.%) milled in a planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; WC vials and WC balls; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating. This is the parent process (proc_ma-35h) of the annealed sample.

processing_steps.atmosphere: argon (quartz tube encapsulated and back filled with argon)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The 35 h milled powder was encapsulated in a quartz tube under argon and annealed at 400 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching, as part of the thermal-stability series (400, 500, 600 and 800 °C, each 1 h + water quench).

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase powder after 400 °C annealing: BCC (ferrite) as the major phase together with γ-brass type and partially ordered B2-type phases (no silicide forms at this temperature).

unmapped_findings: Rietveld refinement of the 400 °C annealed powder (Table 4): refinement quality wR = 2.088, GoF = 1.05, χ² = 1.10; unit-cell volumes BCC 23.39 Å³, γ-brass type 663.05 Å³, B2 24.12 Å³ (no volume field exists for phases in the schema). [b0061]

The 35 h milled powder (parent of this annealed sample) is thermally stable up to ~500 °C; DTA shows two exothermic events at ~420 °C (693 K), attributed to ordering and/or texturing of the γ-brass type phase, and at ~520 °C (793 K), attributed to Fe5Si3-type silicide formation. [b0043, b0112]
The 400 °C annealing was part of a thermal-stability series applied to the 35 h milled powder at 400, 500, 600 and 800 °C, each for 1 h followed by water quenching. [b0023, b0043]
The 400 °C annealed powder was produced by encapsulating the 35 h milled powder in a quartz tube back filled with argon prior to annealing. [b0023]
